# dsh-ctx-visualizer
English | 简体中文
> See exactly what context DeepSeek Harness assembles for every model call — system vs user content,
tool schemas, parsed tool calls, tool executions and the follow-up calls — as a per-turn timeline a
nd a dynamic architecture view.
A community plugin for DeepSeek Harness (tagged `dsh-plugin`), not an official package. It is for an
yone who wants to study the agent loop in detail: inside one multi-turn exchange — *call the model →
parse tool calls → execute tools → feed results back → call the model again* — what exactly was sen
t to the model at each step, what was added compared with the previous step, and which part is growi
o the model at each step, what was added compared with the previous step, and which part is growing.
## Features
After installing, the conversation header gains a **Context Lens** tab:
- **Left · turns**: one card per turn (user question, call count, tool-run count, context tokens, el
apsed time, most-used tools). The column is a fixed-height window you can scroll to reach earlier tu

rns.
- **Top · horizontal timeline**: every step inside the selected turn — `Step 1 · model call → r

uns bash / results fed back → Step 2 …`. Click any node to switch.
- **Right · detail** for the sele

cted step:
- **Architecture** (default): generated dynamically from the actual content — the system
prompt is split into sections by its own headings, tools are grouped by origin (MCP server / built-i
n), and the conversation history is drawn as `user → model call → tool result` chains per user input
, with messages new to this step highlighted and compaction summaries called out. On the right, this
step's flow: request → model → each tool call's outcome/duration/result size → fed back into the ne

xt request.
- **Request context**: shows only the messages *new in this step* by default; system con
tent and the tool list collapse automatically when unchanged; a stacked bar of the context compositi
on (system / user input / tool results / plugin injections / assistant history / tool schemas); inpu

t/output tokens and cache-hit rate.
- **Response** and **Tool runs**.
- **Raw JSON**: the full recor
d plus sub-blocks for system content, user content (user input, tool results, injections) and the mo

del response — all collapsed by default and individually copyable.
- **Persistence**: live captures
are written to `~/.dsh/ctx-visualizer/captures/` and restored after a plugin reload or a Harness res

tart.
- **Backfill**: steps from before the plugin was enabled are rebuilt by replaying the session

log's context changes (including compaction) and marked as *rebuilt*.
- **Redaction**: secrets shape

d like `Bearer …`, `sk-…`, `tos_…`, `ghp_…`, `xoxb-…` are masked before storage.
- **Language**: fol
lows the Harness locale automatically (Chinese/English), with a manual switcher in the toolbar; the
choice is remembered.
## Compatibility
| Item | Version |
| Developed and verified on | DeepSeek Harness Desktop `0.2.0-rc.2`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` `0.2.2-rc.

1` (Web GUI) |
| Node.js (to run the tests) | ≥ 20 |
DeepSeek Harness is still in Developer Preview, so the events and interfaces this plugin relies on m
ay change incompatibly. If something breaks, check the version first and open an issue.
## Install
The plugin has no npm dependencies, so cloning is enough:

Then install that local bundle in DeepSeek Harness, either way:
- **Ask the agent**: say “install the local bundle at `/absolute/path/dsh-ctx-visualizer` with the P

lugin Manager”.
- **Settings page**: Settings › Plugins (if your build supports installing a bundle
*Settings page**: Settings › Plugins (if your build supports installing a bundle from a local path).
`dsh.bundle.patch` in `package.json` is what makes it installable as a bundle; the frontend half is
declared by `dsh.client` and joins the Web GUI automatically.
After installing, **refresh the page** and switch to “Context Lens” at the top of any conversation.
Model calls made after the plugin was enabled are captured live; earlier steps are backfilled from t
he session log automatically.
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
Read-only observation built on first-class Harness events; the agent loop is never modified:
| Event / service | Purpose |
| `llm/stream` (waterfall) | Receives the full `GenerateOptions` of every model request (`messages`,
`tools`, model, …) and collects text, reasoning, tool calls and usage while passing the response st

ream through unchanged |
| `agent/request` | Associates turn / step numbers |
| `tools/execute`, `to
ols/result` | Tool arguments, results, duration and outcome, correlated back to their step by `callI

d` |
| `agent/error` | Records failed steps |
| `sessionQuery.readSession` | Backfill: replays the `
surfaceOp` (append / replace over a seq range) of `system/message`, `user/message`, `assistant/messa
ge` and `tool/result` to reconstruct the context each call received |
The frontend is a `conversation.view` slot plugin that reads the host-side `ctxVisualizer` service o
ver typert Remote. An Inspect Provider named `CtxVisualizer` is also registered so an agent can quer
y capture status with `cordis_inspect_query`.
Every listener is wrapped in try/catch, so a capture failure never affects the agent itself.
## Privacy and security
- Captures are the **full model context** and may contain code, file contents and business data retu

rned by tools. Everything stays on this machine; nothing is uploaded.
- The default redaction only r
ecognises well-known secret prefixes and **cannot** mask every sensitive value. Check before sharing

a screenshot or a copied JSON block.
- Model replies and reasoning text are not redacted yet.
- “Cl
ear captures” in the toolbar also deletes the files on disk.
## Limitations
- Auxiliary calls such as session-title generation and context compaction are not part of the sessio

n log, so they cannot be backfilled (tick “Show aux calls” to see them when captured live).
- File a
ttachments are projected to text in the actual request, so a rebuilt step shows the original attachm

ent blocks.
- Character counts are estimates; for exact token counts, trust the usage reported by th
- Character counts are estimates; for exact token counts, trust the usage reported by the provider.
